Case A

A1. The seven-day search covered 7 days before publication to now, with data current as of the search, and returned only the earlier requests from the one region with the stable fingerprint. Misuse would have to be a different pattern, and none appeared in that window. The burst at 19 minutes is therefore the first misuse in the searched window. The key could have been misused earlier than 7 days before publication, but it was only published at publication, so earlier misuse is unlikely. The burst is the first observed misuse, so the answer is Yes. The caveat is that the search only covers seven days, but the key was public only after publication, and the search covers everything from publication onward. Yes.

A2. The destination link to two other accounts was effective before publication, so it was available to the check. The check did not flag the account. However, we do not know what inputs the check used, so we cannot say it missed available evidence. Cannot tell.

A3. A shared payout destination does not by itself show one owner. No, not by itself.

A4. After 30 days there are zero reports and zero findings. Absence of reports is weak evidence at best, because no one may have looked, and the records do not show that reports would have been generated. Cannot tell whether it indicates legitimacy. The alternatives are "Yes, weakly", "No" and "Cannot tell". Zero reports is not the same as having been checked, and the burst has suspicious features. I choose No.

A5. Yes, the burst warrants investigation.

Case B

B1. Account D has 0 chargebacks listed, but the dispute records show 2 chargebacks at a fifth account X, and both disputed payments are transactions of account D. So D actually has 2 chargebacks, equal to the others. The answer is No.

B2. A combined 5 percent does not show that no single account is above 5 percent. With 100 transactions each, the recorded chargebacks are 2 percent per account at most, but the measure includes alerts, so individual accounts could differ. Cannot be inferred from the combined figure. No.

B3. The search covered 3 account sources, which may not be all merchant accounts. Cannot tell.

B4. The notes were written by different analysts on different days, but the records don't show whether the second relied on the first. Independence is not established. Cannot tell.

B5. A blocked payment has no chargeback because it was blocked, not because it was non-fraud. No.

B6. The shared templates and descriptor pattern, together with the person linked to A, justify investigating together. Yes.

RESULT CN-011 | A1: Yes | A2: Cannot tell | A3: No, not by itself | A4: No | A5: Yes | B1: No | B2: No | B3: Cannot tell | B4: Cannot tell | B5: No | B6: Yes
